high_consensus.description: This is a real determinism gap with a direct contradiction between spec and fixture, and it risks cross-runtime divergence in a critical resolver path. The fix is concrete (lexical classification + rejection rules) and low cost relative to impact.

Valuable operational clarification: stale-cache degraded mode across a fleet can create split-brain behavior. It is actionable but involves more system-level semantics and rollout complexity than a simple spec patch.

Good catch on build-time vs runtime authority boundaries. Without this, generated artifacts can mislead tooling and operators; however, resolving it may require broader artifact-contract decisions across multiple pipelines.

High-value schema migration gap: the common legacy input case has no defined output path. This is highly actionable and essential for safe adoption, with clear acceptance criteria for migration behavior.

Critical and precise: byte-identical cross-runtime gates need a canonicalization standard or they will generate false positives and lose trust. Pinning JCS or equivalent is straightforward and high ROI.
This is a valid resolver edge-case ambiguity with clear behavioral options to specify. It is relatively easy to fix and prevents inconsistent fallback behavior in custom alias scenarios.

blockers.concern: Conflicting wrapper-removal timeline for `model-permissions` (cycle-100 in multiple sections vs cycle-101 MINIMUM in migration section).
blockers.why_matters: Roadmap ambiguity will cause sprint planning churn, broken expectations for downstream tooling, and possible premature deletion of compatibility artifacts.
blockers.recommendation: Publish one authoritative removal date in an ADR, update all sections, and add CI checks against that single policy.

blockers.concern: Degraded read-only fallback can normalize lock-path failures into steady-state behavior.
blockers.why_matters: Operational faults (deadlocks, filesystem issues) may persist undetected while the system keeps running in degraded mode, hiding real reliability problems until a critical config change is needed.
blockers.recommendation: Add hard limits (max degraded duration/count), mandatory alerting, and automatic escalation to fail-closed after threshold breaches.

blockers.concern: Endpoint security controls are specified but not clearly centralized across all HTTP callers (cheval, Bridgebuilder, bash adapters).
blockers.why_matters: If any caller bypasses canonicalization/rebinding/redirect checks, attacker-controlled endpoints can still be reached despite policy intent.
blockers.recommendation: Create a single shared endpoint-validation module and make all outbound model calls pass through it; block direct HTTP client usage in lint/CI.

blockers.concern: Resolver logic is still triplicated across Python/Bash/TS with only fixture-based parity, not shared implementation.
blockers.why_matters: Golden tests reduce risk but cannot cover full state space; subtle precedence drift will still happen over time and cause skill-specific routing inconsistencies.
blockers.recommendation: Define a canonical resolver spec as executable pseudocode or shared library, and generate runtime adapters from it rather than hand-maintaining three implementations.

blockers.concern: Schema migration behavior is inconsistent across runtimes (`schema_version: 1` auto-migrates in Python but is rejected in TypeScript).
blockers.why_matters: The same config can pass in cheval/startup hook but fail in Bridgebuilder runtime, causing environment-specific outages and non-deterministic behavior.
blockers.recommendation: Implement the same v1->v2 migration logic in TS (or remove Python auto-migrate), then enforce identical behavior contract tests for Python/Bash/TS loaders.

blockers.concern: Wildcard endpoint policy (`*.googleapis.com`) combined with operator-controlled endpoints is a high-risk SSRF boundary.
blockers.why_matters: A broad wildcard significantly expands trust surface; if a permitted subdomain is misconfigured/compromised, traffic can be redirected to unintended services while still passing hostname checks.
blockers.recommendation: Replace wildcard hosts with explicit endpoint list per API family, add ownership/change-control for allowlist updates, and pin certificate SAN expectations where feasible.
